excerpts.text:
Golf Course Master Plan

Stan Aldrich addressed the commission speaking in favor of the golf course renovations and
hiring a professional was the right way.

Chairman Strickland thanked Commissioner Hall and spoke in favor of having a master plan
stating it was part of a long-term strategic plan and asked for community support. He thanked
Commissioner Hall.

Commissioner Hall made a motion to accept a proposal from Mike Young Designs Inc. for a golf
course renovation/remodeling master plan. Commissioner Little seconded the motion.

There was a discussion about developing a long-range plan and that the work would be done in
phases, the cost to develop the plan would be $30,000 and the construction would be put out
to bid. There was also conversation about how, last year, golf almost paid for itself, the
potential for working with private investors, and involving stake holders in the planning.

The motion passed unanimously.

money_traces.title: 2023 county governmental funds
money_traces.result: The reported opening balance, income, spending and financing movements reconcile to the closing fund balance.
money_traces.limit: This checks the published accounting totals; it does not establish current bank cash or clear individual transactions.

money_traces.title: Where the 2023 General Fund balance went
money_traces.result: The $5,014,723 reduction is explained by reported spending and financing movements. It is not an unexplained missing-money figure.
money_traces.source_label: County annual report, printed pages 17 and 19
money_traces.limit: Other financing is $695,339 coming in and $4,663,746 transferred out. The beginning and ending amounts are fund balances, not bank-account balances.

money_traces.title: Surface Masters — invoices to checks
money_traces.result: Nine unique checks match eleven invoice amounts, including the retainage release. Two repeated check copies are counted once.
money_traces.limit: Matching a county check copy establishes the recorded payment, not that the check cleared the bank or the work met specifications. This is the supplied packet, not a complete county ledger.

money_traces.title: Surface Masters — contract and final billing
money_traces.period: 2024 LMIG project; payment records through October 24, 2025
money_traces.result: Recorded payments exceed the last supplied change-order contract total by $173,537.06. Unit-price quantity changes may explain some or all of this; the supplied packet does not provide a final approved reconciliation.
money_traces.limit: This is a difference requiring a quantity and authorization explanation, not a finding of theft or overpayment. The final quantity schedule plus lump sums is $4,451,701.42; separately billed Wright Street work is $15,000 gross. That combined $4,466,701.42 is $1,575.01 above recorded checks. The retainage schedule excludes the $15,000 from its lump-sum column, although invoice 1077 includes it. Obtain the final quantity certificate, all revisions, credits and retainage ledger.

money_traces.title: Pittman — 2025 payment gap
money_traces.result: The supplied 109-page invoice/check packet contains older LMIG projects. The three identified 2023 LMIG checks total $1,138,983.74 and cannot be used as payments against the 2025 contract.
money_traces.limit: The older check total is partial history, not a final project cost or a 2025 spending total. Obtain the 2025 project/job number, vendor ledger and corresponding invoices and checks.

money_traces.title: Pittman — approval question identified in county-published report
money_traces.result: The county-published investigator report identifies $1,396,172.95 of changes and $666,245.00 of Board-approved changes, leaving $729,927.95 identified by the investigator as lacking Board approval.
money_traces.limit: This is the investigator’s finding as of the report date. The underlying approvals and any later ratification must be obtained to update it; it does not establish how much of the 2025 contract was paid.

reporting_record.note: County-supplied unsigned Resolution 2026-73 describes monthly cash, obligations and project-spending reports, with the first report due within 30 days of adoption. Verify adoption and request the reports; an unsigned copy does not prove a missed deadline.
